IND.note: World's largest spice producer (~44% of global output, ~12 Mt of all spice crops incl. chilli, turmeric, cumin, ginger, cardamom) and largest exporter. India Spices Board reports record spice-product exports of ~1.8 Mt worth US$4.7bn in FY2024/25; the ~900 kt here is the HS0904-0908+0910 whole-spice slice (chilli/pepper/ginger/cardamom etc.), excluding ground/blended seasoning lines. Also a major re-exporter, importing Vietnamese/Indonesian pepper and Sri Lankan cinnamon for value-add.

CHN.note: Second-largest spice exporter and #2 importer (FAOSTAT/ITC 2024). Dominant in dried chillies/capsicum, ginger and cassia (Chinese cinnamon); ships large volumes to the USA, Spain, Netherlands, Malaysia and the Middle East. Combined-basket estimate across HS0904-0908+0910.

VNM.note: World's #1 black-pepper exporter, ~one-third of global pepper output; ~225 kt pepper produced in 2024 (220 kt black + 30 kt white) worth ~US$1.3bn at record prices (~$5,150/t). Also a fast-growing cinnamon and star-anise exporter. Imports some Indonesian/Brazilian pepper for re-processing. Combined-basket HS0904-0908+0910.

IDN.note: Major exporter of pepper (white pepper from Bangka, black from Lampung), nutmeg/mace (world's largest nutmeg producer), cloves (mostly consumed domestically for kretek cigarettes) and cinnamon (cassiavera). Combined-basket estimate for 2024 across HS0904-0908+0910; FAOSTAT/ITC.

BRA.note: Among the top-5 black-pepper producers/exporters; Espirito Santo and Para drive output. Ships pepper to the Netherlands (EU hub), Vietnam (re-processing), the USA and Middle East. 2024 combined-basket estimate, FAOSTAT/ITC.

MEX.note: Leading exporter of dried chillies/capsicum (HS0904) to the USA — ancho, guajillo, pasilla varieties for the Hispanic/Tex-Mex market. FAOSTAT 2024 importer-reported flow has ~68 kt Mexico-to-USA. Combined-basket figure mainly capsicum.

PER.note: Major paprika and capsicum (aji/piquillo) exporter to the USA and Mexico, plus ginger. FAOSTAT 2024 shows ~40 kt Peru-to-USA and ~17 kt Peru-to-Mexico. 2024 combined-basket estimate across HS0904+0910, FAOSTAT/ITC.

LKA.note: World's largest exporter of true (Ceylon) cinnamon and the 4th-largest cinnamon producer; cinnamon exports worth ~US$217m in 2024 per Sri Lanka EDB. Also pepper, cloves and nutmeg. Sends and receives spice flows with India (cinnamon out, pepper/chilli in). Combined-basket HS0904-0908+0910.

THA.note: Regional spice trading and re-export hub: dried chillies to Pakistan and Malaysia, ginger, plus transit of Myanmar/Indian product. FAOSTAT 2024 shows ~60 kt Thailand-to-Pakistan and ~26 kt Thailand-to-Malaysia. 2024 combined-basket estimate, FAOSTAT/ITC.

MMR.note: Significant exporter of ginger and dried chillies, mostly overland to China and Thailand. FAOSTAT 2024 shows ~21 kt Myanmar-to-China and ~16 kt Myanmar-to-Thailand. 2024 combined-basket estimate; FAOSTAT/ITC. Myanmar under-reports to Comtrade.

MDG.note: World's largest vanilla exporter (the SAVA region supplies the bulk of global natural vanilla) and a major clove and pepper exporter; a fast-growing cinnamon shipper (+67% since 2023). By weight cloves/pepper dominate the basket since vanilla is low-tonnage/high-value. FAOSTAT 2024 shows ~16 kt Madagascar-to-India. Combined-basket HS0904-0908+0910.

NLD.note: Europe's leading spice import, processing and re-export hub (Rotterdam); 3rd-largest world importer by value (~US$253m, ~6.2% of global trade, ITC 2024). Imports pepper from Brazil/Vietnam and chilli/ginger from China, then re-exports cleaned/ground product across the EU (e.g. ~26 kt to Germany, FAOSTAT 2024). Net importer for consumption but huge gross throughput.

USA.note: World's #1 spice importer (~US$466m, ~11.5% of global spice trade, ITC 2024); focus on capsicum/pepper, ginger and Piper pepper. Major suppliers: China, Vietnam (pepper), Mexico/Peru (chilli/paprika), India, Indonesia, Spain. Tiny domestic output (chilli in NM/CA) vs. very large consumption. Combined-basket HS0904-0908+0910.

ESP.note: Major paprika producer (La Vera/Murcia) and a leading EU spice processor/re-exporter; imports Chinese capsicum (~72 kt China-to-Spain, FAOSTAT 2024) and re-exports paprika and blends (~22 kt Spain-to-USA, FAOSTAT 2024). Near-balanced net trade. Combined-basket HS0904+0910.

PAK.note: Large dried-chilli consumer and a major net importer; FAOSTAT 2024 shows ~60 kt from Thailand and ~40 kt from China. High per-capita chilli/spice use. Combined-basket HS0904-0908+0910; FAOSTAT/ITC.

DEU.note: 4th-largest world spice importer by value (~US$232m, ~5.7% of global trade, ITC 2024) and an EU processing/blending hub; sources from China, Vietnam, India and via the Netherlands (~26 kt NLD-to-Germany, FAOSTAT 2024). Negligible domestic production. Combined-basket HS0904-0908+0910.

flows.note: FAOSTAT 2024 detailed trade matrix, importer-reported, HS0904-0908+0910 (combined spice basket). Largest single spice flow in the dataset — Indian chilli/capsicum, ginger and seed spices into China; FAOSTAT importer-reported by China. Plausible given India ~44% of world output and China the #2 importer.

rankings.note: Combined spice basket (HS0904 pepper/chilli-capsicum, 0905 vanilla, 0906 cinnamon, 0907 cloves, 0908 nutmeg/mace/cardamom, 0910 ginger/saffron/turmeric/other), kt, 2024. Exporter order led by India and China is robust (India ~44% of world output, China #2). Importer ranks: USA #1 and Netherlands/Germany as EU hubs are confirmed by ITC 2024 value shares (USA ~11.5%, NLD ~6.2%, DEU ~5.7%); Pakistan/India/Spain/Malaysia tonnage ranks are FAOSTAT/ITC 2024 estimates and approximate because basket weight mixes high- and low-value spices.

companies.name: McCormick & Company
companies.note: World's largest spice and seasoning company by revenue (~US$6.7bn FY2024), owner of McCormick, Schwartz, Club House and Lawry's. Sources pepper, chilli, cinnamon, vanilla and herbs from across Asia, Latin America and Madagascar; runs a global sustainable-sourcing program.
companies.improve: Should disclose origin-country purchase tonnages by spice and progress on its Grown for Good vanilla/pepper sustainability targets.

companies.name: Olam Food Ingredients (ofi) - Spices
companies.note: Major global spice trader/processor as of 2024 (ofi spun out of Olam); large positions in pepper, chilli, onion/garlic and dehydrates, with processing in India, Vietnam and the USA. A key intermediary in the 280 kt+ Vietnamese pepper trade.
companies.improve: Should publish basket-level traded volumes and farmer-traceability coverage for pepper and chilli.

companies.name: Everest Spices (Everest Food Products)
companies.note: One of India's largest branded spice/masala companies; sources chilli, turmeric, cumin and pepper domestically. Faced 2024 regulatory scrutiny (Singapore/Hong Kong) over ethylene-oxide residues, underscoring food-safety stakes in the spice trade.
companies.improve: Should report export tonnage by destination and disclose 2024-onward pesticide/EtO residue-testing outcomes.

companies.name: MDH (Mahashian Di Hatti)
companies.note: Iconic Indian branded-spice and blended-masala maker, a household name domestically and across the Indian diaspora. Like Everest, drew 2024 contaminant scrutiny in export markets. Sources raw chilli, coriander, cumin and pepper from Indian growers.
companies.improve: Should disclose domestic-vs-export split and contaminant-testing protocols post-2024.

companies.name: Synthite Industries
companies.note: World's largest producer of spice oleoresins and value-added extracts as of 2024 (paprika, capsicum, pepper, turmeric/curcumin); supplies natural colours and flavours to global food and beverage majors. Processes a large share of India's chilli and turmeric into extracts.
companies.improve: Should report raw-spice intake tonnage by origin and the share processed into oleoresins vs. whole spice.

companies.name: Nedspice
companies.note: Vertically integrated pepper and spice supplier as of 2024 with a large farmer-partnership program in India and processing in Vietnam; feeds the Rotterdam-centred EU spice trade. A core operator behind the China/Brazil/Vietnam-to-Netherlands flows.
companies.improve: Should publish basket-level traded volume and the share sourced through its farmer-partnership scheme.

global.note: Global spices (combined HS0904-0908+0910 basket: pepper, chilli/capsicum, vanilla, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg/mace/cardamom, ginger and other), kt. Production led by India (~44% of all spice crops, ~12 Mt incl. turmeric/chilli/ginger) then China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Bangladesh. Traded volume recovered to ~4.2 Mt in 2024 (ITC), near the ~4.4 Mt pre-COVID peak; value ~US$4.5bn at ~US$3,350/t average. Output grows ~2-3%/yr.
